title: Loading the demo from the welcome screen can delete a member's own routines and body records without saying so
what: After 'Remove demo data' a member's own routines, body weight, measurements and photos stay on the phone. If they then tap 'Load demo data instead' with no workout of their own, the sheet says only 'You can remove it any time.' and the load erases all of it. With workouts kept, it names only the workouts.

title: Privacy notice says progress photos never leave the phone, but a setting sends them to Google backup
what: With 'Include photos in my backup' on, the newest progress photos are copied into the folder Android backs up to the member's Google account. The privacy notice says the photos never leave the phone.

title: The workout picture's 'more than previous' line can count body weight
what: The share picture leaves body weight out of its kg lifted box, but its 'Workout complete · +N kg more than previous' line is worked out from the full workout total, which counts body weight on pull-ups and dips. When only body-weight reps changed, that number is reps times the member's body weight, on a public picture that says it never shows body weight.

title: Leaving the gym keeps the mobile number a member typed at check-in
what: When a member types a mobile number at check-in, it waits for the desk to confirm. If the member then leaves the gym in the app, the number is cleared from their app record but stays in the waiting request. The owner and front desk still see that request with the number, and approved or declined requests keep the number with no clean-up.

title: The admin app says support looks only when the owner lets them, but MettleUp can open the gym's records alone
what: The owner's 'MettleUp access' card and the Settings page say MettleUp support can look at the gym's records only when the owner lets them. MettleUp's own emergency door opens member names, mobiles, receipts and staff for up to an hour without asking the owner.

title: A real gym named "QA ..." is deleted overnight
what: The nightly clean-up of test gyms picks gyms only by name: any gym whose name starts with capital QA and a space, more than a day old, is deleted with all its members and money records. Nothing stops a real owner from naming a gym that way.

title: MettleUp can open a gym's records without the gym saying yes, while the app promises it never does
what: HQ has an "Open in an emergency" button that opens read access to a gym's members, payments and staff without the gym asking. The gym owner's own screen and the pilot agreement say MettleUp support can look only when the gym lets them.

title: A member back after 3 months who types their first name a little differently loses their saved workouts for good
what: The phone-number backup finds the saved workouts by the number. If that account was not used for 90 days, it opens only when the first name typed now matches the old one exactly (first word, ignoring capitals). "Rahul" then "Raahul", "Dr. Rahul" or a Hindi spelling does not match: the server quietly makes a new, empty account for the number. The member sees "0 workouts brought back", and from then on every sign-in opens the new empty account, so the old workouts can never be reached from the app. Nothing on the name box says the name must match. Members who stop for 3 months and return on a new phone are common in gyms.

title: A member under 18 who was already saving keeps everything on MettleUp's server after the under-18 fix
what: The new under-18 rule only stops new saving. A member aged 10 to 17 who signed in before the fix already has their age, body weight and workouts on MettleUp's server. After the update nothing removes that copy; the only thing that ever deletes it is the member pressing Delete my account. The privacy notice says such data is deleted once MettleUp learns the member is under 18, and the phone does learn it.

title: After an owner gives up a mobile number, whoever later gets that number can set a new PIN and run the gym
what: Forgot PIN sets a new PIN for every owner or staff login that has the mobile number a WhatsApp code was sent to. A person's mobile on the gym can never be changed, so an owner who moves to a new number keeps the old one on file. Indian operators give unused numbers to new customers after a few months. The new holder of that number can ask for a Forgot PIN code, set a PIN and sign in as the owner, with every member's name, phone and payments.

title: A person who paid online when joining shows as not paid on Today once the request is over 45 days old
what: Today's 'Joined online' card lists every open join request, however old. Whether each one was paid online comes from the payment server, which only returns join payments from the last 45 days (and at most 100). For a request left waiting longer than that, the paid payment is not returned, so the card shows 'pay at the desk' with Make member instead of Paid online and Approve, and the warning that stops a second charge cannot see the payment either. The desk can then take the fee again in cash. The test gym has no open join requests, so this was read in the code, not seen.

title: Two privacy fixes are only in the next app version; the app members get from Google Play still has both faults
what: The newest app version on main fixes two open problems: Delete my account now waits for a copy that is still sending, and nothing of a member under 18 is saved on MettleUp's server. Google Play's public page shows version 0.79.0 (updated 25 Nov), one version older, so every member still runs the app where a delete can be undone by a running copy and an under-18 profile is still copied to the server. Both findings are still open, and the release notes leave the fixes out on purpose, so nothing tells anyone they are not live yet.

title: The reply helper in HQ sends a person's help question to Google, but the privacy notice says only Anthropic reads help messages
what: When the owner taps the English helper on a reply, the person's whole help question, the earlier AI answer and earlier team replies go to Google Gemini with the draft. The privacy notice says help questions are read by Anthropic's Claude, and its list for Google names only sign-in, pop-ups, Play and the member-list import. The helper refuses a free Google key, so Google does not train on the text, but the sending itself is not told to anyone. It only happens when the helper's key is saved; whether it is saved on the live server could not be checked.

title: A gym owner's spoken AI Assistant request can go to Sarvam, a company the privacy notice never names
what: When the owner speaks to the AI Assistant, the recording goes first to Sarvam (an Indian speech-to-text company) whenever Sarvam's key is saved on the server; Groq is only the second choice. The privacy notice, in English and Hindi, says spoken requests go to Groq and its list of outside companies has no Sarvam. The spoken request can hold member names, amounts and other gym details. Whether Sarvam's key is saved on the live server could not be checked.

title: A new branch gets the first branch's paid plan, paid-until date and founding Pro for life free
what: When an owner adds a branch, the new branch is given the first branch's MettleUp plan, billing and paid-until date. A gym that has paid for a year gets the new branch paid for the same year without paying for it. A founding gym (Pro for life, one branch) gets Pro for life on every new branch, cannot be asked to pay for it, and each branch also takes one of the 25 founding places. The add-branch sheet only speaks of the free trial.

title: An extra branch is charged full price, but the website promises half price
what: The website and the About page say each extra branch pays half price. When a branch buys or renews its MettleUp plan, the price is worked out from the plan and monthly or yearly only, so a second or third branch is asked for the full price.

title: A workout in progress can be lost if the phone cannot read it back when the app opens
what: When the app opens it reads back the workout that was still going. If that read fails for any reason, the app quietly treats it as no workout, keeps no note of why, and shows nothing. If the member then starts a new workout, the saved one is written over and is gone.

title: The AI's 'no visit in 10 days' counts a member who renewed today after a long break, and its See all opens a list with a different rule
what: When the owner asks the AI who has not come for N days, or taps the 'Not seen for 10+ days' idea, a member who came back today after two months off is counted as 'no visit in 60 days', because the count starts from the last visit before the break, not from the new plan. The See all link then opens Losing the habit, which leaves that member out (and also leaves out anyone whose plan ends within 7 days, whom the AI count keeps). The owner sees one number on the AI card and a different list one tap later, and may send 'we miss you' to someone who paid today.

title: Undo a restore does not stick for a member signed in to MettleUp: the backup's workouts come back seconds later
what: About 8 seconds after a restore, the background copy sends the restored workouts to the member's MettleUp account. If the member then taps Undo (offered on the screen and for 24 hours in Settings), the phone is put back, but the undo also forgets what was copied and asks for a bring-back first. The bring-back finds the restored workouts on the server, sees the phone lacks them, and writes them back onto the phone. The member is told the phone is back to how it was, yet the restored workouts reappear.

title: Help says member messages are deleted after 180 days, but they are only deleted when someone next opens the list
what: The help tells owners that member messages are deleted 180 days after the last one. No timed job does this. Old messages are removed only at the moment the member opens their messages or someone at the gym opens Member messages. If nobody opens either, the old messages stay.

title: Website says our staff cannot open a member list unless the gym lets them in, but HQ can open it in an emergency
what: The gym-owner site says: closed to our staff, they cannot open your member list unless you let them in for 1 hour. HQ has an emergency action that opens read-only access to any gym for 15 to 60 minutes with a typed reason and no OK from the gym. It is logged and the owner sees it afterwards.

title: The complaints contact was promised in both apps, but the member app shows no way to reach it after joining
what: The launch task says the named contact for data complaints goes into the privacy notice and both apps. In the member app the privacy notice is linked only inside the tick box shown once at sign-in or when joining a gym. Settings and About show credits and the version only: no privacy notice, no terms, no contact address. A member who wants to complain about their data later has nowhere in the app to find who to write to.

title: The data agreement says every look at a gym's records is recorded and shown in the admin app, but direct database looks are not shown and may not be recorded
what: The data agreement for gyms and the MettleUp access card both tell the owner that every look is recorded and listed in the admin app. The admin app lists only looks made through a support window. Looks made straight in the database with the owner login are sent by the server in a separate list that the admin app never reads or shows. The notes say this list is not built, that the recording stays off until a logs key is saved in HQ, and that a look made with the server key is never recorded at all.

title: The admin app says a member gets the automatic birthday wish when the member's phone may never show it
what: With the automatic birthday wish on, the AI Assistant and Today stop asking the owner to wish a member whose mobile number and first name match an app member, and say that member gets the wish at 9:30 am. The wish is a notification the member's own phone sets for itself. It does not show when the member turned off reminders from the gym, has notifications off, or has not opened the app lately. The notes also name an older case: a number that was typed but never proven counts as wished in the admin app while the server refuses it. In all these cases nobody wishes the member.

title: Website says MettleUp staff cannot open a gym's member list unless the owner lets them in, but HQ has an emergency button that opens it without the owner
what: The gym-owner home page says, under 'Closed to our staff', that they cannot open the member list unless the owner lets them in for 1 hour. HQ has an 'Open in an emergency' button: MettleUp picks a reason, types a sentence, picks 15, 30 or 60 minutes, and the gym's records open read-only with no yes from the owner. The owner does see it afterwards, with the reason.

title: Website says the AI sees columns only and never sees member details, but the AI is also shown up to 5 example rows from the gym's file
what: The home page card 'Import members with AI' carries the tag 'AI never sees member details' and the demo says 'AI · columns only'. The column matcher is sent the column names and up to 5 example rows of the file. Mobile numbers, emails and ID numbers are hidden and names and addresses are replaced by a placeholder, but the other cells of those rows (plan, fees paid, dates and any extra columns) do go to the AI company.

title: Website says an AI credit is used only when the AI Assistant sends or saves something, but members' AI answers also use the gym's credits
what: The home page says 'A credit is used only when the AI Assistant sends or saves something' and the About page says 'You use AI credits only when the AI finishes a task for you'. The server also takes credits when members get an AI answer to a question: 10 answers use 1 credit, up to the owner's monthly limit. That charge is switched on. Neither page mentions it.

title: Play listing draft says 'Back up to Google Drive', but the app no longer offers a Google Drive backup
what: The Play listing draft tells people they can back up to Google Drive or save one backup file. Since 4 Nov 2026 the app has one backup, the MettleUp account; Google Drive backup is no longer a choice. Only bringing back an OLD Drive backup is still there, and that card is marked for removal around Feb 2027. No screen starts a new Drive backup.

title: Member website promises backup to your own Google Drive, but the app stopped Drive backup
what: The member website says in two places that the app backs up to the member's own Google Drive and brings it all back on a new phone. The app stopped making Google Drive backups on 4 Nov 2026: backups now go to a MettleUp account on MettleUp's server, and Drive is only there to bring back an old backup.

title: 'Your questions' in Help shows one person's questions to the next person on the same computer
what: The list of questions, AI answers and replies from MettleUp is kept in the browser, not per person or per gym, and signing out does not clear it. On a shared desk computer the staff see what the owner asked and what MettleUp replied. The owner's 'delete our gym' request, with the gym's name, code and phone, lands in the same list. A different gym signing in on that browser sees it too.

title: An imported plan named like '3 days a week' becomes a 3-day plan
what: When another software's sheet names a plan by how often the member comes, such as '3 Days a Week Monthly' or '5 days/week 3 months', the import reads the first number and word as the plan's length. The new plan is saved as 3 (or 5) days long, and a row with a start date but no end date gets a membership that ends after 3 days and shows as expired.

title: Past pass visits change when a pass member is edited
what: A check-in the member made by scanning the gym's QR carries no pass company of its own; the panel works it out from the member as they are today. Untick the pass box and every past QR visit of that member leaves the monthly count; tick it again and the first day becomes today, so the old visits stay lost; change the company and the old QR visits move to the new company. The gym then claims too little (or from the wrong company) for a month it has not been paid for yet.

title: Erase can leave reminders and Health Connect on
what: After 'Erase all data', the phone-side clean-up (reminders off, Health Connect sending off, widgets blank, shortcuts gone) runs only after three unrelated screen refreshes. If any of them fails, the clean-up is skipped silently: 'Time to train' keeps arriving, new workouts can still go to Health Connect, and old workout names can stay on the widget.

title: The start-up error screen tells members to send their whole data file to their gym
what: When the app cannot start, 'Save my data file' shares the full phone data (workouts, body weight, notes, profile and mobile number). The line under it says to send the file to the gym, who passes it on to MettleUp. Elsewhere the app promises the gym never gets body weight, photos or notes.

title: Join screen says workouts stay on the phone, then says the gym sees them
what: When the gym has trainers set up, the join card says 'Your workouts stay on this phone.' and, two lines later, 'Your gym and your trainer see your workouts'. Joining then switches trainer sharing on.

title: A member's progress summary is stored again after they leave the gym
what: When a member leaves, their trainer summary is deleted at once. But the three ways the phone sends a summary never check whether the member has left, so the next send from an app that still has sharing on stores the summary again. Nobody at the gym can see it (the lists skip members who left), but it stays on the server until a trainer list is read 90 days later, against the privacy notice's promise that it is deleted on leaving. The gym mate sharing, by contrast, refuses a member who left.

title: Tapping the birthday idea sends members' full names to the AI though the owner never typed them
what: With the automatic birthday wish on, the birthday idea puts 'Send birthday wishes to' plus the members' full names in the request, and a test requires that. Tapping the idea sends that sentence to the AI, so member names leave the gym although the owner did not say them, against what the assistant promises.

title: No test checks that a sign-in code works only once and dies after 30 minutes
what: The screens say a code from the owner works once, for 30 minutes. The server tests check wrong tries and that a new code works, but none uses the same code twice or waits past 30 minutes. The browser tests use a pretend server, so they cannot prove it either.

title: Signing out with a payment the server refused is never tested
what: The only sign-out test with saved items has one waiting check-in. No test signs out while a payment the server refused is kept, signs back in and checks it is still there. No test signs out of a gym with branches, or checks the many-items words.

title: No test proves the gym records leave the device after sign-out or removal
what: Tests check the welcome page and its words after a sign-out or a removal, but none checks that members, payments and the gym name are no longer kept on the device, nor what happens to items still waiting to send.

title: The Workout plans page has no screen test at all
what: No browser test opens Workout plans. Making a plan, sending one to a member, Undo, workout of the day, edit, copy, withdraw and the Pro page are only checked as helper rules and server answers. A broken sheet or button would still pass every test.

title: No screen test shows the desk being stopped from taking cash for a link the member just paid
what: Closing open links before cash, and refusing the cash when the link was paid a moment ago, are tested only on the server and as words in a unit test. No phone test opens Collect payment with an open link, so nobody sees that the sheet stays open with the just-paid words, or that the cash is saved once the link is closed. The offline case, where the check is skipped, is not tested at all.

title: Selling or renewing a PT pack is never done on screen in a test
what: No screen test sells a PT pack. The PT line and its one-session wording, the start jumping to today, the emptied boxes, Renew PT on the PT card, Renew PT hidden for a plan off sale, and a second pack beside the first are checked only as data or not at all.

title: The 'Joined online' card is never tested as the front desk, and its error lines never at all
what: Every Joined online test signs in as the owner. The desk is the one who usually makes these people members, yet no test does it as the desk, checks the receipt names the desk person, or shows the lines for someone else approving, could not approve, could not check the payment, or a name that could not be saved.

title: Adding, editing and retiring a plan is never tested beyond one simple save
what: Plans are only ever added through one helper that fills four boxes and saves. No test checks the wrong-input words (no name, a 1e2 duration, an empty or bad price, a bad joining fee, bad PT sessions), the PT plan switch, editing a price, marking a plan 'Not for sale' and back, or the starter price list. These set what every member is charged.

title: The risky paths of the gym's records card are never tested: unsent money on clear, a failed backup, Cancel on erase
what: Tests check the calm 'Clear offline copy' question only with nothing waiting. The red question that names unsent desk work, a backup that fails ('Could not make the file'), Cancel on 'Erase everything?' and the demo's 'never put online' line are never checked. The backup test checks members and payments in the file but not check-ins.

title: No test proves the microphone and the voice clip stay private
what: Nothing checks that the microphone only starts after Speak, that the clip is removed from the phone after it is sent, or that the heard words stay in the box until the member taps Send. The Settings page version of voice has no test at all.

title: No test proves weight, steps or sleep from Health Connect stay on the phone
what: The app promises body weight, steps and sleep read from Health Connect never leave the phone. No test checks that any of them stays out of what is sent to the gym, a trainer, the server or the AI, or that sleep is kept out of muscle readiness. A change could start sending them and every test would still pass. (The risk of it happening is FN-L4-phone-native-02.)

title: Bringing back a Google Drive backup from the welcome screen is never tested beyond two lines of words
what: No test signs in with Google on the welcome screen, finds a backup, restores it, cancels, finds none, or takes the gym's copy. Only the 'we found your backup' line, the replace warning line and the 18+ tick rule are checked. Nothing checks that only the MettleUp backup file in Drive is read.

title: The phone sign-in privacy promises are tested in the wrong place, so the tests pass while the promises are broken
what: The phone test checks only that Profile shows no mobile number after joining. The number is saved on the member's gym link, which no test looks at. The line 'You pay nothing, and we never message you.' is never checked, and nothing checks that no WhatsApp message goes to the number later.

title: A member linked to the app whose number no longer matches gets neither the app message nor a WhatsApp
what: When the owner sends a group message by asking the assistant, a member counts as 'has the app' if the record is linked to the app OR the mobile number matches an app member. But the app message is only sent to app members found by matching the mobile number. A linked member whose number was changed on the record, or whose app account has no number, is left off the WhatsApp list (they 'have the app') and also left out of the app send (no number match). They get nothing and the card does not say so. If every member of the group is like this, the card says 'Send it on WhatsApp below' with no WhatsApp button under it.

title: 'Send to their app' says 'Sent' even when the member will never get it
what: On Collect payment, the desk can press 'Send to their app' for any member. It always answers 'Sent. They see it under My membership in the MettleUp app.' But the please-pay pop-up only reaches a member whose mobile on the gym list matches the number they joined the app with, who has not left, whose number no other active member shares, and whose phone gave a push address. For everyone else nothing arrives, and the desk waits for money that is never asked for. At Crispy Curves only 1 of 2 members has an app check-in number and 0 of 2 are linked to the app, so at least one member gets nothing while the desk is told it was sent.

title: A renew request stays waiting after the desk renews the member another way, and Approve then sells a second plan as a due
what: A member asks in the app to renew. If the desk renews them from the member page (the usual sell sheet), the request does not learn of it: it stays in Needs you, the bell and the Today card. Approve later checks only for a sale made by that same request, so it sells the plan again, starting after the plan just sold, with the full price left as a due and no question asked.

title: When the workout copy stops saving, the member is told only inside Settings
what: If the member's MettleUp sign-in runs out or the saved copy is full, the copy stops and the phone keeps the workouts only on itself. The app writes one line on the Settings account card and nowhere else: no pop-up, no banner on the Workout tab, no note after a workout. A member who never opens Settings keeps training for weeks believing everything is saved, and loses it all with the phone.

title: A member backed up with Google gets a second, empty backup on a new phone through the WhatsApp check, and cannot switch back once they log a workout
what: Since 25 Nov the phone number check at welcome also signs the member in to a backup account for that number. This is a separate account from the Google one. A member whose workouts were saved with Google (the only way before 25 Nov) proves their number on a new phone, lands in an empty account and is told nothing is saved yet. Nothing links the two or tells them to use Google instead. After they log even one workout, Use Google instead is refused with 'This phone has another person's workouts', and the only way out is to erase the phone.

title: When bringing the saved copy back keeps failing, nothing new is saved and Settings still says the workouts are saved automatically
what: After a sign-in, a restore, an undo or a newer edit from another phone, the copy must first bring the server's copy back before it sends anything. If that keeps failing (sign-in run out, the server down or refusing), each try is only written to the phone's hidden log and nothing is sent. The Settings line is never told: it keeps showing 'saved automatically, last saved' with an old time, 'will be saved in a moment', or 'waiting for the internet', and never 'sign in again'. New workouts can stay unsaved for days while the member believes they are backed up.

title: When a member pays the same request twice online, nobody at the gym is told
what: The payment check and the payment company's notice both go through one step that marks a request paid. When a second, different payment arrives on a request that is already paid, the server keeps it in its own list of seen payments but only writes a hidden log line saying to check the company dashboard and refund it. The desk, the owner and MettleUp HQ are never shown it, so the member's extra money stays with the gym and the gym's books show one payment.

title: Changing the plan on the assistant's add-member card keeps the old joining fee, or none
what: When the owner asks the assistant to add a member, the card fills in the plan's price and joining fee. If the owner then picks a different plan on the card, only the price changes; the joining fee stays at what the first plan had. If the assistant found no plan and the owner picks one, the joining fee stays at zero. The card shows one total price with no fee line, and the checks allow it for the owner, so a member can be saved owing a wrong joining fee.

title: When a desk computer cannot send cash or a new member, only that computer knows
what: If the gym server refuses a payment, a new member or a check-in that a desk saved without internet, or the desk cannot keep it at all, the reason goes only into the browser's hidden log on that one computer. The automatic crash reports catch only errors nobody handled, so these never reach MettleUp. An owner on another phone does not see the held cash either.

title: After a slow connection, 'Try again' on a member import can drop those members' plans and payments
what: When a batch of new members is sent but the answer never comes back, the import marks those rows as not saved and offers Try again. If the save had in fact landed, Try again now finds them already in the gym and calls them 'Already a member.' Their plans and payments from the old software are then not sent at all, and the row is no longer marked as waiting, so nothing tells the owner the money history is missing.

title: MettleUp is never told when members' workout copies stop saving
what: The app reports crashes to MettleUp, but a copy that fails without crashing is written only to the phone's own log, which nobody reads in a real app. A server change that breaks saving, a copy refused as full or too big, members needing to sign in again, or a bring-back that keeps failing all stay on the phone. Every member could have a stuck backup for weeks and MettleUp would learn of it only when someone loses a phone and complains.

title: The outage alarm never checks WhatsApp sign-in codes or the AI service
what: The 10-minute alarm only asks whether the websites, HQ, the gym server and the backup answer. Nothing scheduled checks that WhatsApp still delivers sign-in codes or that the AI service still answers; the WhatsApp check exists only as a hand-started run to the owner's own phone. If WhatsApp refuses MettleUp's number or template, members cannot sign in by phone and MettleUp hears about it from a gym.

title: If WhatsApp number checks stop working, owners cannot reset a PIN or start a gym and MettleUp hears only from the gyms
what: Forgot PIN and the new-gym number check depend on WhatsApp. When Meta stops delivering codes or stops sending us the person's message (a payment block, a paused template, a changed secret), each failure is only a log line. Nothing counts failures or alerts anyone, so owners stay locked out until one calls MettleUp.

title: The AI Assistant gives a lower profit for the month than the Expenses page, because it leaves out shop sales
what: The Expenses page counts shop orders handed over this month as money in, next to fees. When the owner asks the AI Assistant for this month's profit, it adds up fees only, while still taking off the stock bought for the shop. A gym that sells supplements sees a smaller profit, or a loss, in the assistant than on the Expenses page for the same month.

title: When a staff member leaves, cash he took without internet and never sent stays on his phone, and nobody is told
what: Payments, plans sold and new members made with no internet wait on the device that made them. When the owner removes a staff member who leaves, that person's phone loses its sign-in, but the waiting payments stay on it and are sent only if someone from the same gym signs in on that very phone again. The owner's Remove box says 'Your members and payments stay as they are', and the removed person's screen only says 'You no longer have access'. Neither says that money taken on that phone has not reached the gym's records, so the receipts are missing from dues and money totals with no warning.

title: A member who left and comes back through an Excel import gets his new plan but stays hidden as archived
what: When the owner imports a list and a row is a member the gym archived earlier, the import screen says "Already a member (name, archived)". The plan and payment on that row are still saved to him, but he is never brought back from the archive, whichever duplicate choice the owner picks. So a returning member has a paid, running plan, yet he is missing from the Members list, the Active members and ending-soon tiles, and every message group, while his money shows in Collections.

title: Approving an app pause can hand free days to a member whose plan ends before the pause starts, or has already ended
what: A member can ask in the app to pause any days starting up to 90 days ahead, as long as their plan has not ended on the day they ask. The pause does not have to fall inside the plan. When the desk taps Approve, the full number of paused days is added to the end of the plan, with no check that the plan still runs or that the pause starts before it ends. So a member whose plan ends on 25 Nov can ask to pause 1 Dec to 28 Feb; Approve moves the end to late February and he trains for three months free. A request left waiting until after the plan ended is approved the same way. The card shows only the pause dates, not when the plan ends, so the desk has nothing to warn them. The Bring a friend reward, by contrast, refuses a plan that has ended.

title: When the plan lock is switched on, a gym whose free trial ended long ago goes straight to read-only with no warning days
what: The plan lock gives a gym 7 grace days and then 30 basic days after its trial or paid time ends, and only then makes it read-only. It counts those days from the old end date, not from the day the lock is switched on. Gyms made before billing existed were told nothing locks when a trial ends. Any such gym whose trial ended more than 37 days before the switch is flipped wakes up read-only: no new members, nothing saved but looking and downloading, without ever seeing a grace or basic warning.

title: Undoing a second import file leaves a member owing money they never owed
what: When a second import file adds payments to a plan that an earlier import made, it raises that plan's price to match. Undo this import then removes the second file's receipts but keeps the raised price. The member's page and the dues list then show money owed equal to the removed receipts, though the member owes nothing.

title: A member with a personal training pack sees the pack's last day in their app as their plan's last day
what: The sell sheet sells a personal training pack beside the gym plan, and the admin panel keeps the two apart: the member's status, 'ends in N days' and renewals follow the gym plan only. The member's app does not. It takes whichever plan covering today ends last, pack or gym plan. So a member whose gym plan ends in 5 days but whose 3-month pack runs on sees the pack's name and its far-off last day, gets no 'renew soon' line and no 'plan ends soon' reminders, while the panel lists them as ending. The other way round, when the gym plan ends last, the app hides the pack's sessions left. A pack sold to start later counts as 'a plan paid ahead' and switches off all plan-ending reminders.

title: A personal training pack changes the member's plan end on the phone but not in the admin app
what: The admin app never lets a personal training pack decide when a member's gym plan ends. The member's phone does: it takes whichever plan covering today ends last, and any plan starting later, personal training packs included. So a member whose gym plan ends on 30 Nov but who has a training pack to 31 Dec sees 'ends 31 Dec' on the phone and gets no plan-ending reminder, while the admin app shows 'Ending in 1-3 days'. A training pack bought to start next week also counts on the phone as a renewal already paid, so every plan-ending reminder is skipped.

title: An imported plan with its price in the name becomes a plan hundreds of months long
what: When another software's sheet names a plan with its price before the length word, such as '999 Monthly', 'Rs 1500 monthly' or '1200 Yearly', the import reads the last three digits of the price as the plan's length: 999 months, 500 months, or 200 years. A row with a start date but no end date then gets a membership that runs for decades, so the member never shows as due for renewal, and the new plan of that name is saved with that length for future sales.

title: A person who paid when joining online and is then marked lost is reported as a member who may have paid twice
what: Self-join pay online is live. If the desk marks a paid online joiner as lost on Enquiries instead of pressing Approve, the gym holds their money but they are not a member. The 'Paid online, receipt not made' card then says they 'were made a member without Approve' and 'may have paid twice', and tells the desk to save the payment on their member page. There is no member page and no Open member button, and nothing says the money should be refunded.

title: Undo import removes members who already joined the member app or were measured at the desk
what: When the owner undoes a past import, a member counts as 'used' (and is kept) only after a check-in, a desk payment, extra days, an edit or a PT session. A member who has since linked the MettleUp member app, had weight and body fat measured, got a door-machine number, or was sent a workout or diet plan is still removed. Their app link, measurements and machine number are left pointing at a member who no longer exists, and the screen says 'Nothing you added yourself is removed.'

title: A member who renewed or came in at the desk can still get 'your plan ends' or 'we haven't seen you' reminders
what: The gym's automatic reminders are set on the phone days ahead, from the plan and last visit the phone knew when the app was last opened. The 15-minute background check does not refresh them. A member who renews at the desk, or is checked in by the desk, and does not open the app, still gets 'Your plan ends tomorrow', then 'Your plan ended on ...', or 'We haven't seen you for 14 days', while the admin app shows a paid renewal and a recent visit. The test gym has desk check-ins, so this mix is real.

title: The member app can show a personal training pack as the member's gym plan
what: My membership in the member app takes whichever plan running today ends last, and treats any plan starting later as a paid renewal. A personal training pack counts for both. The admin app never lets a PT pack decide the member's gym status while they have a gym plan. So a member whose gym plan ends on the 30th and whose PT pack ends on the 15th of next month sees the PT pack, 'Ends 15 Dec', no 'Renew at the desk' line, while the admin app puts them on the renewals list. A PT pack bought to start later hides the renew line and stops every plan-ends reminder on the phone. Turned the other way, a gym plan ending after the PT pack hides the PT sessions count and the 'PT running low' reminder. The test gym has no PT packs, so this was found by reading the code, not on data.

title: Add member says only the gym's staff can see a member's photo, but the photo goes into MettleUp's nightly copy too
what: Under the photo on Add member the desk reads that only the gym's staff can see it. The photos are kept in an ordinary table of the main database, and the nightly backup copies every such table, so each photo also sits for 7 days in MettleUp's own storage, where anyone with MettleUp's cloud login can open it and no look is recorded. The backup's own note still says member photos are not in a copy. The photo switch is not on live yet, so no real photo is exposed today.

title: The gym-owner site and the members' notice say member data is kept in India, but a full nightly copy sits with Cloudflare outside that promise
what: The gym-owner website says 'Your member data is stored in India' and 'Data kept in India (Mumbai)', and the short notice gyms copy for their members says MettleUp has 'servers in Mumbai, India'. But every night a full readable copy of the gym database is written to Cloudflare's store for 7 days, and the privacy notice itself lists Cloudflare's location as 'many countries, including India'. The web server's own small database (payment records, form questions) has no India location set either.

title: Owners can add a door machine today, but the address it is told to call does not exist, so it never comes online
what: Settings > Entry machines is open to every gym on the live panel, because its database part is live. The owner adds a finger or face machine by serial number and is told to set the machine's server address to gate.mettleup.fit, with 'It shows Online within a minute'. That address has no live service: the door service was never put live and the address does not even resolve. The machine stays 'not seen yet' for good, no member is let in by it, and the screen never says why. The 'not ready for your gym yet' message only shows when the database part is missing, which it no longer is.

title: The phone-number backup is recorded as released on 25 Nov, but no app with it has gone out
what: The newest What's new entry and the server change both say 'phone number sign-in also keeps your workouts safe' went out on 25 Nov. The server half is live, but no new app was released: Google Play, the app's own news file and the newest GitHub release all still show 0.79.0 a day later. Phone number is the main way to sign in, so every member who signed in that way still has no copy of their workouts on MettleUp's server and loses them with the phone, while the notes say this is fixed.

title: The outage alarm checks about every 6 hours, not every 10 minutes
what: The alarm that should notice when the website, the gym panel, HQ or the gym server stops answering is set to run every 10 minutes, and the notes and the feature map say it does. In real life GitHub starts it only about 4 times a day: over 1 to 26 November the gap between checks was 6 hours in the middle case and almost 12 hours at worst. A gym panel outage in the evening rush can last hours before anyone is told.

title: Every member is offered 'Install on watch', but the watch app is only on Google Play's test tracks
what: Settings, Phone and watch, Your watch shows 'Install on watch' to anyone whose watch lacks MettleUp, and it opens the watch's Play Store on MettleUp. A code switch says the watch app is on Play. But Play shows the watch app only on its test tracks, with nothing in production. So a normal member who taps Install, or searches the watch Play Store as the app suggests, finds nothing. The MettleUp Plus page also lists 'MettleUp on your watch' as a paid feature.

title: Both websites offer the free watch app, but the watch app is not out on Google Play for the public
what: The member site says 'Free on Wear OS watches' and 'The free MettleUp watch app works on Android (Wear OS) watches', and the gym-owner site says the same. In Play Console the watch app has no public release at all: it is only on internal and closed testing tracks, and the open testing version is waiting to be published. A visitor who reads the site and looks for the watch app on Play cannot get it. This is also a claim an ad regulator would count as misleading.

title: If the AI key goes missing, or one usage table cannot be read, the AI Assistant quietly disappears for every owner
what: The server answers 'switched off' when the AI key is not set, and also when a usage table cannot be read. The admin app then hides the AI Assistant with no word to the owner. A missing key is not even logged, so nobody at MettleUp is told. The assistant also borrows the help box's key when its own is missing, so one lost key can stop both.

title: After a gym disconnects its shop, members can still place orders that nobody will ever see
what: Disconnect the shop only makes this browser forget the gym's key. The gym, its code and its products stay switched on on our server, so members who joined can keep ordering (and, where paying online is on, paying). The owner no longer has any screen that shows those orders, and the screen says only that members and payments are still here.

title: The nightly backup never copies member photos, workout report files or gym logos
what: The nightly copy holds every table but none of the stored files. If the database project were lost, every member photo taken at the desk and every workout report file would be gone for good; the restore guide says so, but nothing else copies them.

title: Reports from 'Report this page' are saved where nobody can read them, and HQ has no button to take a page down
what: A visitor who reports a gym web page as a scam, offensive or closed gets a thank-you, and the report is stored. But nothing in HQ, the HQ server or any other part of the product ever reads those reports, and HQ has no way to take a page down: it can only show whether a page was taken down. A scam or offensive page stays up and nobody at MettleUp ever hears of the report.

title: A gym that pays for Starter while on Pro never moves to Starter while online buying is off
what: When HQ confirms a Starter payment for a gym still on Pro or in its trial, the gym is told Starter starts on the day Pro ends. Only the nightly billing job makes that switch, and that job runs only when online buying is switched on, which it is not. So the gym stays on Pro for ever at the Starter price, and its admin app keeps showing a Starter start date that has passed.

title: Deleting a gym leaves its payment company keys and payment records on our web server
what: When HQ deletes a gym, only the gym server and its files are cleared. Our separate small web database still keeps that gym's sealed payment company keys or sign-in tokens, every payment link record with member ids and amounts, and its AI limits. The keys are only wiped after a desk presses Disconnect, which a leaving gym may never do. Nothing removes the payment records at all.

title: Anyone can get another 3-month free trial by making a new gym with the same mobile
what: Create my gym gives every new gym 3 free months unless a WhatsApp-checked number is sent. The number check is behind a switch that is off, and the panel falls back to making the gym without it. So an owner whose trial ended can make a fresh gym with the same number, import his members again, and use Pro free for another 3 months, as often as he likes (5 gyms an hour from one internet address).

title: A front-desk login can let any member train free for ever by ticking "Comes with a pass"
what: On the add or edit member form, the front desk can tick "Comes with a pass" and type any company name. That member then never shows as expired, drops off the renewal list and the expiring numbers, and the entry machine is told to let them in with no end date. Nothing on the server stops a desk login from doing this, and no owner approval or alert follows. A desk person can turn a friend or a lapsed member into a free member; the owner sees it only if they read the Pass visits page and notice a company that pays nothing.

title: A stranger who types a member's mobile number when joining the app gets the gym's messages meant for that member
what: When someone joins a gym in the member app, the server keeps whatever mobile number the join sends, with no check. The admin app then treats that number as proof of who the person is: the App members list opens the real member's page for them, a message sent to a member or a group (from Messages or the AI Assistant) is delivered in the app to anyone whose join number matches, and the real member is marked as already on the app, so the WhatsApp list leaves them out. The server itself no longer trusts a typed number for check-ins (the desk must confirm it), but the admin app still does for messages. Today's app sends no number at join, so this needs someone calling the server directly with the gym code and a member's number.

title: Anyone with a free Google account can park about 1 GB on our server through the workout copy
what: Signing in with Google is open to everyone, gym or not. The saved copy of workouts takes up to 30,000 pieces of up to 32 KB each per account, about 1 GB, at 200 pieces a call with no daily cap. A few throwaway Google accounts and a small script could fill the shared database that every gym uses, or run up the storage bill.

title: Through our own server address every person looks like the same sender, so sign-in and new-gym limits hit everyone at once
what: Both apps reach the gym server through MettleUp's own address, so a supabase.co block in India cannot stop them. The gym server's limits on wrong PINs (5 per number in 15 minutes) and on new gyms (5 per network address in an hour) count by the sender's network address. Through our address, Cloudflare hands the gym server one shared address for every person (Cloudflare documents this for a Worker calling another Cloudflare site). So anyone who knows an owner's or desk person's mobile can type 5 wrong PINs and lock that person out for 15 minutes, again and again; and after 5 new gyms are made in any one hour, every further new-gym sign-up that hour is refused as busy. A guesser who calls supabase.co directly is not slowed by honest users, but honest users are slowed by him.

title: HQ cannot erase one member: the step says to do it through support access, which can only read
what: A delete request for one member tells the owner to open support access, find the member and erase their details by hand. Support access is read-only, and HQ has no erase button for a member. The only thing HQ does is tick the request as done, and the tick does not check that anything was erased. So a member's erase request can be closed as done with the member's details still in the gym's records.

title: A gym cannot erase a member's details, though the data agreement says the gym handles erase requests
what: The admin app has no way to delete or blank out a member. Its list of record actions has undo for an import, a check-in and an expense, but nothing for a member. The gym server also refuses to delete any member, plan or receipt typed in by hand; only imported ones can be taken back. The data agreement tells the gym that when a member asks to erase their details, the gym handles it. So a gym that gets such a request has no tool to do it, and HQ has none either (already written for HQ).

title: A deleted record keeps all its details on the server for ever
what: When the panel deletes a record (an undone import of members and receipts, a check-in, an expense), the server only marks it deleted and keeps the whole record, with the member's name and mobile, hidden but in the database. The first version of this step blanked the record; a later version dropped that, and nothing cleans these rows later. So an owner who undoes a wrong import believes those people are gone, but their details stay on MettleUp's server and in its backups.

title: After a gym goes online, its old browser copy of every member stays on that computer for ever, even after sign out
what: When a gym kept in one browser is put online, the browser's own copy of the gym (all members, mobiles, plans, payments and check-ins) is moved aside under a dated name and is never deleted. Signing out clears the online copy but not this one. The privacy notice says signing a device out deletes the copy the admin app keeps on it. On a shared front-desk computer this full member list stays behind, unseen, after the gym has left or the staff member has gone.

title: The desk can add a child as a member, with photo, birthday and address, while the privacy notice says MettleUp holds no data of anyone under 18
what: Add member accepts any date of birth that is a real day and not in the future, so a 12 or 15 year old can be added with a desk photo, mobile, address and emergency contact. Nothing warns the desk, asks for a parent's yes, or marks the member as a child. These records sit on MettleUp's server. The privacy notice says MettleUp is only for people aged 18 or over and that data of anyone under 18 is deleted once known, yet here the birthday itself tells MettleUp the person is under 18 and nothing deletes it. India's data law asks for a parent's checkable yes before a child's data is handled.

title: The member-list import shows Google's AI real names from some columns, while the privacy notice says names are hidden
what: Before up to 5 example rows of a gym's old member file go to Google Gemini (or Claude), name and address columns are swapped for a placeholder. But a column whose heading holds a word such as trainer, coach, no, number, ID, code or from is always sent as it is, even when its cells are people's names. So a 'Trainer' column, a 'Father / Guardian name and contact no' column, an 'Emergency contact name (mobile no)' column or a 'Referred by member ID' column sends real names (mobiles stay masked). A free-text remarks column that does not look like a name or an address, such as 'BP patient since 2020', is also sent word for word, so health notes can go out. The server repeats the same rule, so it catches none of this. The privacy notice says names, addresses, mobiles, emails and ID numbers are hidden and only plan names, amounts and dates are not.

title: A person who only asked about joining can never be removed from the gym's enquiry list
what: The Enquiries page lets the owner or desk mark someone "Not interested", but there is no way to delete an enquiry. The server refuses to delete any enquiry, so the name, mobile number, question, follow-up notes and reason stay on MettleUp's server and in its backups for as long as the gym uses MettleUp. These people never became members. If one of them asks the gym to erase their details, the gym cannot do it, though the data agreement says the gym handles erase requests. India's data law also asks that details be erased once their purpose (a possible sale) is over.

title: A gym that turns its shop off, or starts its demo over, leaves its members' names and shop orders on our server for ever
what: A gym kept only in the browser can turn on the shop. That makes a real gym on MettleUp's server with a gym code; members join it with their name and place shop orders there. 'Disconnect the shop' (and, for a demo gym, 'Start over') only makes this browser forget the key. The gym, the members who joined and their orders stay on the server, nothing deletes them later (the nightly clean-up only removes test gyms named 'QA ...'), and the owner has no button left to delete them, because 'Delete the gym' is offered only to gyms that are online. The screen does not say the server copy stays.

title: Delete my account says everything on MettleUp's server is deleted, but a gym member's workouts shared with the gym stay
what: Before and after the delete, the app tells the member that their account and everything saved on MettleUp's server is deleted. The delete only removes the saved copy, the member's account and its profile. For a member who is in a gym, the trainer summary of their workouts, their leaderboard totals, machine use, shared workouts and questions to a trainer all stay on MettleUp's server, because they hang off the gym link, not the account. When the account is kept because the gym also uses that sign-in, the older activity summary and the profile stay too, while the screen still says everything saved on MettleUp is deleted. The privacy notice gets this right (leave the gym to delete those), but the app's own words do not.

title: A member who turned on photo backup can no longer find the switch to turn it off
what: The 'Include photos in my backup' switch now sits on a page that no Settings row opens. A member who turned it on earlier keeps it on: at every app start and after every new photo, the newest progress photos are copied into Android's backup to their Google account, and the Progress photos page even says their newest photos are in the phone's backup. There is no way in the app to stop it except erasing everything.

title: Phone sign-in says the number is not kept, but after joining the gym it is saved on the member's gym link
what: The phone sign-in screen says 'Your number is checked once and is not kept for this', and the privacy notice says the same. When the member then joins the gym the search found (by tapping Join, or going straight in), the app hands the proof in and the server writes the proven number, twice, onto the member's link to that gym, with the time it was checked. It stays there until the member leaves, and another finding shows leaving does not clear the check-in copy. The gym already has the same number on its member list, so no new party sees it, which is why this is not marked S1; but the words promise something the system does not do.

title: The privacy notice says the trainer summary holds 3 months of workouts, but the app now sends up to a year
what: When sharing with trainers is on, the app sends the gym every workout since the member joined, up to the last 12 months and up to 400 workouts, each with its name, every exercise's heaviest set and how many sets. The app's own caption says 12 months. The privacy notice, in English and Hindi, still says the summary holds up to 30 workouts from the last 3 months.

title: Sharing that starts on its own at joining rests on legitimate interest, a reason India's data law does not have
what: Joining a gym switches on three kinds of sharing without a yes: workouts for trainers, which machines are used, and the pop-up code. The privacy notice gives legitimate interest as the reason and says the member can object. India's data protection law allows personal data use with consent or for a short list of legitimate uses; it has no general legitimate interest. The workout sharing goes to the gym, which can see a member's training history for a year.

title: A gym cannot erase a member from the server, so a member's request to the gym to erase their details cannot be done
what: The privacy notice tells a member who left to ask the gym to erase the rest of their details. The server refuses to delete any member, plan, membership or receipt the gym typed in by hand; only imported ones and check-ins can be deleted, and even then the row keeps all its details with a deleted mark. A member who leaves the app keeps their name, join date and leave date in the gym's app list for good; only the mobile number is cleared. Their shop orders keep their name too. Nothing in these files removes any of these rows while the gym stays on MettleUp. HQ has no erase tool either (written down separately).

title: Workout offer dates and the list of who joined are only deleted when the owner opens the offers page
what: The privacy notice promises workout offer dates go 90 days after the offer ends, and the record of who joined and left goes 1 year after. The deleting only runs when the owner opens the workout offer page or saves an offer. The nightly clean-up does not touch these. A gym that stops using offers keeps every member's counted workout dates and offer history with no end.

title: When a member joins a gym, the server keeps no record that they agreed to the notice or said they are 18 or over
what: The privacy notice says a member first ticks that they are 18 or older and agrees to the notice and terms before joining. The join on the server takes only the gym code, a name and an optional number; it keeps no record of the tick, the notice version or the time. So MettleUp cannot later show that a given member agreed, or to which version. The workout offer and the owner's terms both keep such a record; the member join does not.

title: The time limits the privacy notice gives for gym-shared data only run when someone opens that screen
what: The notice promises that leaderboard numbers go after 62 days, machine use after 63, workouts shared with gym mates after 60, the trainer summary after 90 days without an update, questions to a trainer after 180 days, and a sent workout report after 30. No timed job does any of this. Each clean-up runs only for one gym, and only when a member or staff person of that gym opens the matching screen. In a gym that stops using a feature, or stops using MettleUp, the data stays with no end. Machine use is also skipped while the gym is paused. Leaving the gym still deletes a member's rows at once, so this hits members who stay.

title: Deleting a member from the gym's list leaves their photo and body measurements behind, out of sight
what: The desk photo and the body measurements are saved under the member's id on the gym's list. When the gym deletes that member from its list, nothing removes them. The screens only open a listed member, so the gym no longer sees that they are still there. Only a whole gym delete removes them. The face photo and the body figures stay with no end date.

title: Trainers now get a year of a member's workouts, but the privacy notice still says 30 workouts from 3 months
what: Since 14 Nov the member's phone shares up to 400 workouts from the last 12 months with the gym's trainers, with the best weight, reps and sets of up to 20 exercises each. The privacy notice tells members the trainer summary holds up to 30 workouts from the last 3 months. Members agree to a much smaller share than the one that really happens, and the sharing is on by default when they join.

title: The privacy notice says nothing about the join-online form or the gym's web page, which collect names, numbers and questions
what: People who are not yet members can fill the gym's join-online form (name, mobile, gender, plan, a health tick) or ask the gym a question from its web page (name, mobile, question), and later chat with the page's AI helper. Their details go into the gym's enquiry list, and MettleUp also keeps its own copy of the mobile number. The page asks them to tick a consent, but the privacy notice lists only MettleUp's own demo form and the friend invite page. Nothing tells these people what is kept, for how long, or which outside AI reads a chat.

title: The delete-account page says nothing is on our server unless you used Continue with Google, but joining a gym or signing in with a phone number puts data there
what: The page Google Play links to for account deletion says you only have an account if you tapped Continue with Google, and that otherwise nothing is saved on our server and there is nothing to delete. The privacy notice repeats it for EU and UK readers. But a member who only joined a gym with its code has their name, leaderboard numbers, trainer summary, machine use and pop-up code on the server, and phone-number sign-in (added 15 Nov) does not need Google at all. The email route also only works from the Google email address, so such a member is told there is nothing to ask for and has no way to ask. The page was last changed on 10 Nov, before phone sign-in.

title: A plan HQ sets by hand can be switched back to Starter overnight by an older Starter payment
what: When a gym pays for Starter while Pro (or the free trial) is still running, the system plans a switch to Starter for later. If HQ then sets the gym's plan by hand (for example Pro yearly after a payment), that planned switch is not cleared. On the planned day the nightly job moves the gym to Starter anyway, although HQ set Pro. HQ never shows that a switch is planned.

title: Cash taken offline that the server later refused disappears from the member's dues and the money counts
what: When a payment taken with no internet is refused once it is sent, it is kept only in the warning bar at the top. The member's page goes back to showing the full amount still owed, the 'payment still being sent' block no longer stops a second payment, the Today line of money waiting to send leaves it out, and the clear-offline-copy warning does not name it as money. The member already paid and holds a printed receipt.

title: When the app cannot close a member's open payment link, the desk payment is saved anyway and the link can still be paid
what: Before saving cash or UPI on Collect payment, the app asks the server to close any open online payment link for that due. If that ask fails (no internet, the server or payment company does not answer), the app carries on, saves the desk payment and says nothing. The link the member already has stays open, so they can pay the same due a second time. Today payment links are test mode only, so no real money moves yet; it bites once live payments are switched on.

title: After live payments start, an old test connection still shows Connected and payment links quietly fail
what: A gym that connected Razorpay or Cashfree during test mode keeps a green Connected badge once MettleUp switches live payments on, and the Test mode label disappears. The server no longer makes links with a test connection, so the desk taps Make a payment link and only reads that the link could not be made, try again. Nothing tells the owner to connect again with live keys, and Paste keys is hidden while it shows Connected.

title: A member who paid twice shows as more than due, with an I saved it button and no word about a refund
what: If the desk takes cash for a due and the member then pays an old online link, the payment comes in late and lands on Today under Paid online, receipt not made, as more than what is due. The card asks the desk to save it by hand and tap I saved it. It does not say the member has paid twice and is owed money back, although the app knows the link was paid after it was closed.

title: A person who paid online when joining still shows "Not paid yet" on Enquiries, and Add as member there lets the desk charge them again
what: On the Enquiries page, every online join request says "Not paid yet.", because the gym server always saves it as unpaid; the real online payment is kept elsewhere. Add as member on that page opens Sell membership with the whole fee due, does not close the person's open payment link, and gives no warning. Only Today's Joined online card checks the payment and offers Approve. So the desk can take the fee in cash from someone who already paid online, and the person can still pay online after paying at the desk. The money check later says "They may have paid twice".

title: An owner who paid MettleUp by UPI or bank transfer can never open the receipt for it
what: When MettleUp confirms a UPI or bank payment, the server makes a numbered receipt for it. The only list that shows these receipts sits inside the Pay online part of the Pay MettleUp screen, and that part asks the server nothing while online paying is switched off, which it is. So the owner sees Confirmed, paid until a date, but no receipt anywhere. The receipt page itself tells them to open it from Your receipts, which they cannot see.

title: A shop order the member already paid online looks unpaid on the Shop page, and Collected says the money was just taken
what: When a member pays for a shop order in the app, the server keeps a list of shop orders paid online so the Shop page can say Paid online. Nothing in the admin app reads that list, and the paid-online sweep skips shop payments. The order card looks exactly like an unpaid one and still offers the pay-by-QR or link box. Once the payment is marked paid, the check before Collected only warns about a payment found paid at that very moment, so tapping Collected (paid) shows Order N collected, Rs X taken. The desk can take cash for an order that was already paid.

title: A shop order paid online can be cancelled, by the gym or the member, and nobody is told to give the money back
what: The gym's Cancel order sheet says the items go back into stock and the member sees Cancelled. It never checks whether the member already paid online and says nothing about a refund. The member can also cancel their own order in the app while it is new, even after paying. Cancelling does not close the order's open payment link either, so a saved link can still be paid for a cancelled order. The money stays with the gym's payment company with no record that it is owed back.

title: A member who already paid for MettleUp Plus can be shown the buy buttons again and charged a second time
what: The app decides whether to show the buy buttons only from what it remembers on the phone. After Erase all data it forgets the purchase and only asks Google Play again the next time the app is started fresh; the same happens when Google Play did not answer at start. In that gap the member sees the monthly, yearly and for-life buttons again. A member with the for-life plan who taps monthly, or a monthly member who taps for life, is charged again by Google Play, and nothing warns them. A monthly member who taps yearly is told Thank you and the app then says they pay every year, while Google Play keeps charging every month.

title: After the owner changes the gym's UPI ID, members are still shown the old one to pay
what: Each payment asked of a member (a fee, or a shop order) keeps the UPI ID the gym had on the day it was made. When the owner saves a new UPI ID, only the gym's setting changes. A member's open fee and any open shop order keep showing the old QR, the old Pay by UPI app link and the old ID to copy, for up to 30 days, and a shop order reuses that same request each time the member taps pay. Money sent that way goes to an account the gym may no longer use, or to a staff member's old ID.

title: In test mode, a real gym owner who pays with a test card gets a real paid plan and a real receipt
what: Buying a MettleUp plan online only works with the payment company's test keys today. But the payment it takes is treated like real money: the gym's paid-until date moves on, the plan changes, and a numbered MettleUp receipt is made. The owner's billing screen and receipt never say test mode. The switch that opens Pay online is one switch for every gym, so turning it on to try it with the test gym opens it for every gym, and any owner could get a year of Pro with a test card.

title: An owner whose payment could not become a plan is told nothing
what: When the payment company takes the owner's money but it cannot become a plan (the amount was not what was asked, or the gym changed in between, for example it went Pro for life on another link), the money is kept for MettleUp to refund or set by hand. The owner's billing screen still shows the old plan and end date, no receipt, and no word that the payment arrived and is being checked. Only the MettleUp office list shows it.

title: Test-mode payments are announced to members and gyms as real
what: Member payment requests and payments made while payments are still in test mode (no real money) go out like real ones. A member gets a phone pop-up saying their gym asked them to pay their fee, tap to pay. The gym's alert bell says the member paid online, see it on Money. Neither says test mode, though each payment request knows whether it was test or live.

title: While payments are in test mode, the member app shows a test payment as paid, but the gym records nothing
what: Payments are in test mode for every gym today, yet any gym that connects Razorpay or Cashfree has the member app pay switch on by default. Members then get test payment pages for their dues and shop orders. A member who finishes one sees Paid, thank you (or Paid. The gym can see it. for a shop order), while no money moved, the gym's Shop page does not show the order as paid and the due stays open at the desk. The join page and the gym web page are kept away from test payments on purpose; the member app is not.

title: The nightly backup builds the whole database as one answer, so it will stop working once the data gets big
what: The nightly backup reads every table, every row, into one single answer inside the database and sends it in one go. The database has a hard size limit for one such answer (a few hundred MB), and the whole copy must also fit in memory and in one call's time. Workout cloud copies and check-ins grow every day, so at some point the backup will fail every night, and there is no way to take it in pieces.

title: The Cloudflare free-limit warning comes once a week, after the busy day has passed
what: HQ looks at Cloudflare's daily request count only on Monday night, for the week before. A day that runs past the free daily limit on a Tuesday stops every MettleUp app until 05:30, and HQ only says so the next Monday. Only requests are watched; other free Cloudflare limits are not.

title: Payments waiting to be sent can be wiped by the browser when the device runs low on space
what: Payments, check-ins and new members taken with no internet wait in the browser's own store. The panel never asks the browser to keep that store for good and never checks how much space is left. Under low space a browser may clear a site's store, taking unsent receipts with it, and the desk gets no warning beforehand.

title: Member photos are kept inside the main gym database with no cap per gym, so they eat the free 500 MB limit that every gym shares
what: Each photo taken on Add member is saved as a picture of up to 100 KB (about 60 KB aimed) inside the same database that holds every gym's members and receipts. There is no limit on how many photos one gym keeps, and photos of deleted members stay behind. About 8,000 photos across all gyms would fill the free 500 MB on their own. When the database is full, saving members and payments can stop for every gym at once. Every screen that shows faces also pulls the photos through the database, which uses the free download traffic.

title: Each admin panel on screen asks the server every minute, so under a hundred busy gyms can use up the free daily request limit for everyone
what: While the admin panel is in view, the Needs you check asks the server once a minute, and reads its other lists every five minutes. A desk that keeps the panel open through a 16-hour day makes over a thousand requests. The free Cloudflare plan allows 100,000 a day for all gyms together, so roughly 80 to 90 such desks fill it, and then every gym panel and member app stops answering until the day resets.

title: Anyone can start demo gyms and upload photos with no total limit
what: Starting a demo gym needs no sign-in and gives an owner key; up to 300 new gyms an hour are allowed across the whole project, each with a ready-made shop. Each gym can hold 50 upload tickets at once, and one ticket lets in any number of 3 MB photos for 15 minutes. Nothing limits how much one gym stores in total, and demo gyms are never cleared unless their name starts with 'QA '. One person could fill the shared free database and picture store for every real gym.

title: One member account may store about twice the whole free database in its workout copy
what: Anyone who signs in with Google gets a server copy that is capped only by row count (30,000) and by size per row (32 KB). Together that is close to 1 GB for a single account, while the whole free database is 500 MB and is shared with every gym. Nothing caps the total bytes per member or how fast one account may write. One damaged or misused phone could fill the database and stop every gym's desk from saving.

title: A very long workout is silently left out of the saved copy while Settings says everything is saved
what: A workout or other item bigger than the copy's size limit per item is skipped and only noted in the developer log. It never joins the waiting count, so the backup line in Settings says the workouts are saved. On a new phone that workout is missing.

title: Once 1,000 help messages arrive in a day, every member's message is refused and nobody at MettleUp is warned
what: The help and feedback box takes at most 1,000 messages a day from everyone together. After that every member who writes in, even about a real problem, reads "Too many messages today" and the message is not saved. There is no warning to the team before or when this happens.

title: One gym can fill the shared database through record saving, with no total limit or speed limit
what: Each save of gym records may carry up to 1,000 records of up to 20 KB each, about 20 MB in one go. Nothing limits how often a gym saves, and nothing limits how much one gym keeps in total. Removed records also stay on the server. Any owner key may do this, including the key a demo gym gets with no sign-up. A broken device or a misuser could fill the free 500 MB database that every gym shares, and then every desk stops saving.

title: Some ways an Aadhaar number could slip into an import are never tested
what: No test fixes a row under 'Rows to check' and checks the ID number is still cut, imports the same file twice and compares, writes an Aadhaar in Hindi digits or odd separators, or checks that the skipped-rows download has no ID number. The on-screen promise line and the 'read as usual' line are never checked.
